title: RFID Fish Tag (PIT) — ISO 11784/11785 + ISO 24631 / NMFS PIT / PTAGIS / USFWS + AFTM / AALAS / FELASA / AVMA PIT Tag Welfare Aquaculture & Fisheries Research
summary: Passive Integrated Transponder (PIT) fish tags deliver individual identification across aquaculture broodstock, fisheries research, and endangered-species programmes. ProudTek supplies HDX and FDX-B ISO 11784/11785 + ISO 24631-1/-6 conformance-tested transponders in 8.4 × 1.4 mm micro, 12 × 2.12 mm standard, 23 × 3.85 mm bolus, and 32 × 3.85 mm long-range formats — matched to the reader, antenna, and detection-station infrastructure that the Columbia River PIT Tag Information System (PTAGIS), NMFS Endangered Species Act programmes, USFWS refuge monitoring, NOAA Fisheries stock-assessment work, and the AFTM (American Fisheries Society + American Fisheries Society Fish Marking Techniques Committee) reference. Chip options include Texas Instruments HDX (RI-TRP-RRHP), {chip:em-microelectronic-em4305:name} / EM4469 / EM4569 FDX-B, and Biomark / Oregon RFID / Destron Fearing-compatible encoders. Welfare posture follows AFS/AIFRB Use of Fishes in Research, AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia of Animals (2020), AALAS / FELASA aquatic-species guidance, and the 2% body-weight tag-to-fish ratio rule. Biocompatible medical-grade borosilicate glass + Parylene-C anti-migration coating; EO-sterilised pre-loaded single-use injector needles (12 g / 14 g / 16 g); retention >98 % at 6 months when body-cavity injected per PTAGIS protocol. Export posture covers CITES Appendix I (sturgeon, European eel) + II (Atlantic salmon listed stocks) aquaculture traceability, EU 2016/1012 zootechnical + EU 2019/1009 + EU CFP (Common Fisheries Policy) catch-documentation, and US Magnuson-Stevens Act stock-rebuilding programmes.

sections.title: Regulatory context: PIT tagging in US and international fisheries research
paragraphs: Individual-animal identification in aquaculture and wild fisheries science converges on ISO 11784/11785 LF transponders operating at 134.2 kHz, with the ISO 24631 family adding the conformance (ISO 24631-1) and performance (ISO 24631-6) envelope that receiver / transponder suppliers cite. In the United States, NMFS / NOAA Fisheries conducts Endangered Species Act Section 7 and 10(a)(1)(A) research under USFWS permits; the Columbia River PTAGIS network — operated by the Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission — ingests tens of millions of annual detections from Bonneville, McNary, John Day, Lower Granite, and Ice Harbor smolt-monitoring arrays, with data feeding the Comparative Survival Study and Smolt Monitoring Program under Magnuson-Stevens Act rebuilding plans.

The American Fisheries Society Fish Marking Techniques Committee (AFTM) + AFS/AIFRB Use of Fishes in Research jointly govern welfare expectations: the core threshold is that tag mass must not exceed 2 % of fish body mass, and injection protocols must include anaesthesia (MS-222 or AQUI-S 20E), aseptic technique, and post-tagging recovery monitoring. AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia of Animals (2020) and AALAS / FELASA aquatic-species guidance cover the IACUC documentation that university and agency programmes rely on.

International programmes add CITES Appendix I (sturgeon Acipenseriformes, European eel Anguilla anguilla) and Appendix II (Atlantic salmon listed stocks, giant clam, humphead wrasse) traceability requirements; EU programmes add the Common Fisheries Policy (Regulation 1380/2013) catch-documentation framework + EU 2017/625 Official Controls + EU 2016/1012 Zootechnical Regulation. FAO publishes the Code of Conduct for Responsible Fisheries and the Aquaculture Certification Council operates third-party audits.

sections.title: Welfare & 2% body-weight rule — AFS Use of Fishes in Research

dataHighlight.heading: AFS welfare threshold: tag-to-fish mass ratio must not exceed 2 %
dataHighlight.text: The American Fisheries Society + American Institute of Fishery Research Biologists Use of Fishes in Research guideline, together with AFTM practice, caps PIT tag mass at 2 % of fish mass. The 1.4 × 8 mm micro tag weighs ~0.03 g — inside the threshold for fish as small as 1.5 g (≈55-60 mm fork length for salmonids). The 2.12 × 12 mm standard tag at ~0.10 g hits the 2 % threshold at fish ≥5 g (≈80-100 mm). Tagging below the threshold impairs swimming performance, predator avoidance, and energetic balance, and AVMA 2020 + AALAS / FELASA aquatic guidance reinforce that anaesthesia (MS-222 / AQUI-S 20E), aseptic technique, and recovery monitoring are non-negotiable.
dataHighlight.source: American Fisheries Society + AIFRB Use of Fishes in Research (2014, updated 2020) / AFTM Fish Marking Techniques / AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia of Animals 2020 / AALAS / FELASA aquatic-species IACUC guidance

sections.title: Operating playbook — aquaculture and fisheries programmes
paragraphs: Atlantic / Pacific salmon hatcheries running selective-breeding broodstock commonly specify 8.4 × 1.4 mm FDX-B micro PIT tags body-cavity injected at 55-60 mm fork length, with DNA parentage genotyping cross-referenced against the 15-digit ISO ID. AquaGen, Hendrix Genetics Aquaculture, Stofnfiskur, Benchmark Genetics, and Genus Aquaculture all operate broodstock programmes built around individual-animal tracking across multiple generations, with estimated breeding values calculated in AquaManager / Fishtalk and confirmed at harvest weighing with Biomark / Oregon RFID / Destron Fearing handheld readers.

Wild-salmon ESA research under NMFS Section 10(a)(1)(A) permits commonly specifies 12 × 2.12 mm HDX tags for PTAGIS-compatible detection. Bonneville / McNary / John Day / Lower Granite / Ice Harbor dam-bypass arrays read smolts on outmigration; upstream antenna suites on Idaho / Oregon / Washington streams read returning adults. The Comparative Survival Study and Smolt Monitoring Program ingest detections into PTAGIS for Magnuson-Stevens Act rebuilding-plan analytics. AFS Use of Fishes in Research welfare protocols and AVMA 2020 anaesthesia guidance gate the IACUC permit.

Sturgeon (Acipenser spp.) and European eel (Anguilla anguilla) programmes — both CITES Appendix I — commonly specify 23 × 3.85 mm long-range tags for juvenile stocking and 12 × 2.12 mm micro tags for eel post-elver life stages. Traceability from hatchery to harvest is a regulatory precondition for international trade; the ISO 11784/11785 15-digit ID + Lacey Act + CITES documentation chain is routinely audited.

Tilapia / striped-bass / catfish commercial aquaculture commonly specifies 12 × 2.12 mm FDX-B standard tags for growth-rate trials, feed-formulation work (Skretting NUTRACE + Cargill iQuatic + Pharmaq Analytiq), and stocking-density optimisation. Individual weight-gain telemetry feeds Xpert Sea / Manolin / Aquabyte growth-model dashboards and Pharmaq / Zoetis Fish Vet Group vaccine-trial efficacy analysis.

Ornamental-fish and koi high-value-specimen programmes commonly specify 12 × 2.12 mm FDX-B tags for insurance (high-value specimens at EUR 100k+), theft prevention, and pedigree registration with breed societies. The AAHA Universal Pet Microchip Lookup does not cover fish directly, but pedigree associations (All Japan Nishikigoi Promotion Association, ZNA) maintain their own 15-digit ID registries keyed to the ISO transponder.

sections.title: Automated detection-station architecture
bullets: Flat-plate antennas — horizontal or vertical mount at raceway outlets, pond drains, tank drains; 30-70 cm read range depending on HDX vs FDX-B.
Pass-through loop antennas — circular loop in-stream; fish swim through; 60-90 cm detection volume; HDX-preferred for Columbia River PTAGIS stations.
Multi-antenna array readers — Biomark IS1001-MTS, Oregon RFID multi-antenna HDX reader, Destron Fearing FS2001-ISO; simultaneous detection across 4-16 antenna lanes.

Solar + cellular remote stations — Campbell Scientific dataloggers, cellular modem uplink, PTAGIS-compatible file format; enables PTAGIS + regional-monitoring integration at remote stream sites without grid power or fiber.
Fish-ladder / dam-bypass integration — built into Bonneville / McNary / John Day / Lower Granite / Ice Harbor smolt-monitoring systems operated under NMFS ESA permits.

faq.question: What is the minimum fish size for PIT-tag injection under the AFS welfare rule?
faq.answer: The 1.4 × 8 mm micro PIT tag (~0.03 g) can be body-cavity injected into salmonids as small as 55-60 mm fork length (≈1.5-3 g), maintaining the AFS Use of Fishes in Research 2 % tag-to-fish mass threshold. The 2.12 × 12 mm standard tag (~0.10 g) requires fish ≥5 g (≈80-100 mm). For fish below 55 mm, visible implant elastomer (VIE) or alphanumeric visible-implant (VI) marks are the pre-tagging interim. AVMA 2020 + AALAS / FELASA protocols require MS-222 or AQUI-S 20E anaesthesia plus aseptic technique; IACUC approval is required for university and agency programmes.

faq.question: How does a PTAGIS-compatible station differ from an aquaculture tank reader?
faq.answer: PTAGIS-spec Columbia River detection uses 12 × 2.12 mm HDX tags read through in-stream pass-through loop antennas (60-90 cm detection volume) paired with Biomark IS1001-MTS, Oregon RFID HDX-2, or Destron Fearing FS2001-ISO multi-antenna readers. Solar + cellular remote stations with Campbell Scientific dataloggers upload detection records in the PTAGIS-compatible file format. Aquaculture tank / raceway systems typically use 12 × 2.12 mm FDX-B tags with flat-plate or tunnel antennas (30-50 cm range) integrated into AKVAgroup Fishtalk, Pentair Select, or Pharmaq Analytiq growth / feed-conversion dashboards.

faq.question: What regulatory documentation covers sturgeon and European eel aquaculture PIT tagging?
faq.answer: Sturgeon (Acipenseriformes spp.) is listed under CITES Appendix I, which requires a complete hatchery-to-harvest traceability chain for international trade; European eel (Anguilla anguilla) is listed under CITES Appendix II. In the US, Lacey Act (16 USC §3371-3378) traceability + USDA APHIS VS Form 16-4 / 7001 + USFWS 50 CFR Part 17 cover import/export. In the EU, Regulation 1380/2013 (CFP) catch-documentation + EU 2017/625 Official Controls + EU 2016/1012 Zootechnical cover aquaculture supply-chain audits. The ISO 11784/11785 15-digit unique ID + ISO 24631 conformance + performance certification forms the identifier backbone.

faq.question: Does PIT tagging affect fish growth or survival?
faq.answer: Published research across dozens of species (summarised in AFS Use of Fishes in Research 2014, updated 2020) confirms that properly injected PIT tags do not significantly affect growth rate, swimming performance, or survival when tag mass is under 2 % of fish body mass. Short-term (24-48 h) procedural mortality is typically <1 % with an experienced operator using aseptic technique and AVMA 2020 anaesthesia protocols. Retention exceeds 98 % at 6 months when body-cavity injected per PTAGIS-referenced protocol. EO sterilisation per ISO 11135 (SAL 10^-6) + ethylene-oxide residual testing per ISO 10993-7 eliminate post-injection infection risk.
